answer: The juniper storage haven activates each earning identity only while it answers synchronized random probes against its own 100 GB key-salted replica; missed probes suspend rewards. Identity-bound encoding and concurrent deadlines stop one replica serving many aliases, so each extra identity requires another 100 GB and read bandwidth. Stored shale survey archives supply the data. This assumes encoding resists compression and on-demand reconstruction; wealthy operators can still buy more capacity.
